items.statement: Among patients aged 75 and over with complicated discharges, an attended family meeting with a written plan is associated with lower odds of unplanned readmission within 30 days (adjusted odds ratio 0.6 or lower) after adjustment for case complexity.
items.rationale: Need is high because a hospital-wide policy and social work time depend on the answer; novelty is moderate because trials exist but local routine meetings are untested; feasibility depends on note reading.
items.risks: Residual confounding by family conflict or engagement; readmissions to other hospitals are missed.

items.statement: Booked meetings that the family did not attend are not associated with readmission once complexity is adjusted for.
items.rationale: A contrast between attended and unattended bookings helps separate the effect of the meeting from the selection of complex families.
items.risks: Few unattended bookings may give a wide interval.

items.statement: Any association is concentrated in patients who live alone.
items.rationale: Patients living alone depend most on a plan that family members understand.
items.risks: Subgroup finding with little power; reported only as exploratory.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected, h2 kept as a pre-specified contrast, h3 exploratory.
